answer: Each agent can post proposals freely, but rewards come only after a random audit: an agent must reveal a secret committed before the task, and a randomly selected peer checks its work against a public rubric. The protocol bonds payment until the audit passes and slashes the bond for fabricated evidence. Sybils can multiply identities, but they cannot cheaply multiply honest, independently useful work: each fake needs a costly bond and credible output. A plume of accounts may color the ocean of proposals like pigment, yet earns nothing without passing scrutiny.
